sglearning.report:
Our short videos hold people far better than our long ones. Most shorts were 37–66% watched, while the long videos managed only 9–13%.
The long videos lose about half their viewers in the first 35 seconds. The intros repeat the same point and say 'let's see' instead of getting going.
Best: the Sahara refund short. It was 66% watched on YouTube, and only 36% swiped it away on Instagram, compared with 55–84% for the other Reels.
Weakest: the ₹500 SIP long video. It was only 9% watched, and just 3 of every 100 viewers reached the end.
Shorts whose second sentence gave a hard fact (a name, a year, a big number) kept almost everyone; the ones that described a scene instead lost 13–23%. Five videos had too few or no YouTube views to judge yet.
The one change this week: the first two sentences of every video must ask one clear question and back it with a real name or number, with no warm-up.

arthvan.report:
1. Shorts hold far better than long videos: the long ones lose 57% of viewers in the first ~40 seconds, and only 2-4% watch to the end.
2. Best: the Jagannath flag short. 326 views, people watched 157% of it on average (they replayed it), and 120% were still there at the end.
3. Openings about a character doing something shocking (Surpanakha, Prayagraj Hanuman, Jatayu) lost 38-43% of Instagram viewers in 3 seconds; ritual 'why' openings (Tulsi, Karna) lost 57-65%.
4. Weakest: the Tulsi short. 65% swiped it away within 3 seconds on Instagram.
5. Five new videos have no YouTube numbers yet; Jatayu already reached 1,047 Instagram views, our best reach this week.
6. The one change: start every video with a person doing something surprising, and save the answer for the end.
